draft.title: Prehistory and history
card: the time before people used writing. We know about it mostly from archaeology, which studies objects and places that people left behind.
in the narrow sense, the time covered by written records. The first writing appeared about 5,000 years ago.
Archaeologists dig up tools, bones, buildings and art. These show how people lived, but they cannot give names or the exact words people said.
Writing began at different times in different places. So the end of prehistory was not at the same time everywhere.
draft.remember: Prehistory is known mostly from objects. History in the narrow sense is known from written records.

a.q: Which source would mostly be used to study a society in prehistory?
opts: Stone tools and bones dug up at a campsite
A king's letters written on clay tablets
A law code carved into a stone pillar
A diary kept by a traveller
a.why: Prehistory is the time before writing, so it is known mostly through archaeology, such as tools and bones. The other three are written records, which belong to history in the narrow sense.
a.clue: Prehistory is the time before writing.

b.q: A team finds a village with houses, pots and graves, but no writing of any kind. What does this mean for the people who lived there?
opts: They are studied as prehistory, using the objects left
They cannot be studied, because there are no records
They are studied only by reading the words of others
They lived after history began, so are studied by texts
b.why: With no writing, the village is studied through archaeology, as prehistory. Objects can still tell us a lot about how people lived, so the lack of writing does not make study impossible.
b.clue: Objects can still be evidence, even without words.

a.best: Stone tools and bones dug up at a campsite

b.best: They are studied as prehistory, using the objects left
